test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 11 Feb, 2026 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
In the given figure, AB is parallel to CD. What is the value (in degrees) of x?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/314838c5680b15280e48bf5d6d5a4153c2d75588f96837fbd20a18b8cb762dd7.png]
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For parallel lines with an interior kink, the angle x is the sum of the supplementary interior components.

Angle x = (180° − Angle BAE) + (180° − Angle DCE)

x = (180° − 120°) + (180° − 140°)

x = 60° + 40° = 100°

**∴ The correct answer is 100°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

AB || CD

Angle BAE = 120°

Angle DCE = 140°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/71f29efc055717ec0bdf48a6fd7a3d91e61c6c14165345275af910a751ed1068.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Draw a line EF parallel to AB passing through point E.

⇒ Since AB || CD and EF || AB, then EF || CD.

⇒ Angle BAE + Angle AEF = 180° (Co-interior angles between parallel lines AB and EF)

⇒ 120° + Angle AEF = 180° ⇒ Angle AEF = 60°

⇒ Angle DCE + Angle CEF = 180° (Co-interior angles between parallel lines CD and EF)

⇒ 140° + Angle CEF = 180° ⇒ Angle CEF = 40°

⇒ x = Angle AEF + Angle CEF

⇒ x = 60° + 40° = 100°

**∴ The correct answer is 100°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Co-interior Angles

When two parallel lines are cut by a transversal, the sum of the interior angles on the same side is always 180°.

Alternate Interior Angles

When two parallel lines are cut by a transversal, the alternate interior angles are equal (e.g., Z-shape angles).

Transitivity of Parallelism

If line L1 is parallel to line L2, and line L2 is parallel to line L3, then line L1 is also parallel to line L3.
